summary: Robert P. Scharlemann worked in religious studies and philosophy after studying at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University. He held positions at the University of Southern California (~1965–1966), University of Iowa (~1966–1981), and University of Virginia (~1981–1999).

Robert S. Ellwood specialized in religious studies and Japanology. After studying at the University of Colorado, Yale University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, he served on the faculty at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).

Robert S. Nelson is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at Rice University and New York University. He held posts as professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and later at Yale University (~2005–2021).
Robert S. P. Beekes worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Leiden University under F. B. J. Kuiper. He held posts at the Marnix Gymnasium and later at Leiden University in 1973 and 1979.
Robert Sewell worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1868 to 1894 and held the post of Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives.

Robert Seymour Conway worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at the City of London School (~1879–1883), he held posts at Newnham College (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).
Robert Warren Clark is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1994, he was attested studying under doctoral supervisor Karen C. Lang and adviser and teacher K. L. Seshagiri Rao.

Robert Zimmermann worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at St Beuno's and Humboldt University of Berlin, later serving as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and head of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robert Zydenbos specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. After studying at Utrecht University (~1974–1983), he held posts at the University of Toronto, University of Munich (~2003), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
Robert van Gulik was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1929–1930) and completed his doctoral studies under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (~1930–1935).

Robin Coningham works in archaeology and Indology. After earning his PhD at Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin, he held chairs at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (appointed 2005).
Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University (~2005).

Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School, Magdalen College, and completed his doctorate under John Hurrell Crook (~1969–1974). He held an academic post at University College London (~1987–1994).

Philosopher Roderick M. Chisholm studied at Brown and Harvard. He held posts at the Barnes Foundation (~1946), Brown University (~1947–1987), and University of Graz (1974), alongside serving as president of the Metaphysical Society of America (1973).
Roderick S. Bucknell worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Queensland (~1976–2002), where he served as an associate professor from ~1995 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he was attested as professor emeritus in 2011.

Roger Brown worked in linguistics and related fields. After completing his undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Michigan between ~1945 and 1952, he held a long-term academic post at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.

Roger Caillois worked in philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Marcel Mauss, he served at the United Nations from ~1948 to 1971.

Roger Heim studied at École Centrale Paris (~1920–1923) and the Science Faculty of Paris (until 1931). He spent his career at the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle (~1929–1970), serving as its director from ~1950 to 1965.

Roger R. Jackson studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology at Wesleyan and the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He spent his main academic career at Carleton College (~1989–2016), serving as Associate Professor of Religion.
